title: Model count reads 0 / 18 when the local engine install is skipped - the check is gated on an engine that will never exist
description:
Found live 2026-07-30 by the user on the real 1.3.0 portable extract, first run, MPI-390 RunPod escape hatch taken. At first run he pointed the models folder at G:\CubricModels, which holds real weights across diffusion_models/, checkpoints/, loras/, text_encoders/, vae/ and more. The home hero still reads MODELS 0 / 18. His objection is the right one: the app knows where his models are because it just asked him, so an on-disk count should not require an engine.

ROOT, and it is structural rather than a bad render. The models root has TWO sources of truth and the install check can only see one of them. syncModelInstalled() is subscribed to the engine:ready event at js/shell.js:1465, and that subscription carries its own explanation - 'check models only after engine is set up - this ensures extra_model_paths.yaml exists before we try to read it'. On the server side getCustomRoot() at routes/shared.js:423 reads base_path out of extra_model_paths.yaml, and that yaml is resolved with getComfyPath(ENGINE_ROOT, ...) - it lives INSIDE the engine. routes/engine.js:519 is what writes it, during the post-install step of a local engine provision.

So when MPI-390's 'Skip the local engine install' is on: no engine is provisioned, no extra_model_paths.yaml is written, engine:ready never fires, syncModelInstalled never runs, and /comfy/models/check would have had no root to stat even if it had. The count is not wrong - it is the untouched initial 0 from heroStats.js:47 _renderModels(installedCount = 0). The folder the user chose at first run is stored and then never consulted by the install check.

DO NOT FIX THIS ON THE COUNTER. Patching heroStats or firing syncModelInstalled unconditionally would just move the failure - the server resolver still has no root without the yaml. The real question is whether the first-run models-root choice should be persisted independently of the engine (app-level setting) with extra_model_paths.yaml written FROM it rather than being its only home. That also decides what the Model Library shows on a cloud-only machine before any Pod is connected.

SCOPE NOTE: a cloud-only user is the exact population MPI-390's escape hatch was built for, so this is that user's FIRST impression of the app - it says zero models on a disk that has models. Also check the remote twin per the engine-split rule: on a connected Pod the check runs against the volume, so the local-disk count may be wrong there too.
acceptance: Decide the product question first: is the first-run models-root choice an app-level setting that outlives the engine, or does it stay engine-owned
With 'Skip the local engine install' ON and a models folder holding real weights, the home hero reports a truthful installed count without any engine present
The Model Library is coherent on a cloud-only machine before any Pod connect - either it lists what is on disk or it states plainly why it cannot
extra_model_paths.yaml is still written correctly when a local engine IS later provisioned, from the stored root rather than instead of it
Both engine paths checked - local and remote-connected - per the engine-split sweep rule
